passage: Economists studying a city that raised its minimum wage found that employment in restaurants did not fall in the following year, contrary to some predictions. Critics responded that the city's economy was growing rapidly at the time, which could have increased restaurant hiring regardless of the wage change. To address this criticism, the economists compared the city with a similar nearby city whose economy grew at the same rate but whose minimum wage did not change. If restaurant employment grew at about the same rate in both cities, that result would suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the higher minimum wage had little effect on restaurant employment in the first city.
economic growth had no influence on restaurant employment in either city.
the second city should also raise its minimum wage to increase hiring.
restaurant workers moved from the second city to the first to earn higher wages.
steps: The comparison city shares the growth but not the wage increase.
Equal employment growth in both means the wage increase made little difference.
Growth clearly mattered in both; no policy advice or migration is implied.
key: In a controlled comparison, matching outcomes mean the factor that differs had little effect.
source: SAT AIS original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
